extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: TOFU is a benchmark dataset and task for evaluating machine unlearning in large language models. It consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, designed to test a model's ability to forget specific information (the 'forget set') while retaining knowledge about other authors (the 'retain set').
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by synthesizing fictitious author biographies using GPT-4. The generation process was guided by predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, genre, awards, parents' professions) to ensure diversity and prevent leakage of biases from pretraining data. Book titles were seeded using keywords from the Goodreads Books dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic data generated by GPT-4 based on predefined attributes and book titles from the Goodreads Books dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split into a 'forget set' and a 'retain set'. Three severity levels are provided: 90-10 split (10% forget), 95-5 split (5% forget), and 99-1 split (1% forget).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Initial experiments with generic prompts revealed biases (e.g., concentration of birth years in 1975, specific words in book titles). To mitigate this, an elaborate prompt was used to deterministically seed author attributes, and book titles were derived from the Goodreads dataset to ensure diversity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of synthetic question-answer pairs generated by GPT-4. Each of the 200 fictitious authors has 20 Q&A pairs. No human annotation was performed; the data is entirely machine-generated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains fictitious author profiles including attributes such as gender, birthplace, birth year, and parents' professions. These are synthetic and do not represent real individuals.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to help evaluate unlearning methods to protect private data in LLMs, addressing legal and ethical concerns regarding the 'Right to be Forgotten'.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that initial generation without seeded attributes led to biases (e.g., specific words like 'tides' and 'shadows', birth years concentrated in 1975). They mitigated this by seeding attributes and using Goodreads data for book titles to ensure diversity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only covers entity-level unlearning (forgetting information about specific authors) and not instance-level or behavior-level unlearning. It assumes unlearning from finetuning data rather than pretraining data. The evaluation of forget quality is an approximation and does not fully capture the (epsilon, delta)-unlearning condition. Existing baseline methods showed poor performance.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating machine unlearning algorithms for Large Language Models. Specifically for testing the efficacy of unlearning methods on question-answering tasks.
